senses.definition: (transitive) To follow behind (someone or something); to tail (someone or something).
examples: The hunters trailed their prey deep into the woods.

senses.definition: (transitive) To drag (something) behind on the ground.
examples: You'll get your coat all muddy if you trail it around like that.

quotes.text: Our little life is but a gust That bends the branches of thy tree, And trails its blossoms in the dust!
quotes.reference: 1896, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, The Poetical Works of Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, page 287:

quotes.text: "I saw your brother—I saw your brother," he said, nodding his head, as Archer lagged past him, trailing his spade, and scowling at the old gentleman in spectacles.
quotes.reference: 1922 October 26, Virginia Woolf, chapter 1, in Jacob’s Room, Richmond, London: […] Leonard & Virginia Woolf at the Hogarth Press, →OCLC; republished London: The Hogarth Press, 1960, →OCLC:

examples: He walked into the house, soaking wet, and trailed water all over the place.

senses.definition: (transitive) To show a trailer of (a film, TV show etc.); to release or publish a preview of (a report etc.) in advance of the full publication.
examples: His new film was trailed on TV last night.
There were no surprises in this morning's much-trailed budget statement.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To hang or drag loosely behind; to move with a slow sweeping motion.
examples: The bride's long dress trailed behind her as she walked down the aisle.

quotes.text: Even now I behold a sign, A threatening of wrath divine, A watery, wandering star, through whose streaming hair, and the white Unfolding garments of light, That trail behind it afar, The constellations shine!

senses.definition: (intransitive) To run or climb like certain plants.

quotes.text: The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the round windows.
quotes.reference: 1954 July 29, J.R.R. Tolkien, “I: A Long-Expected Party”, in The Fellowship of the Ring (The Lord of the Rings; 1), →ISBN:

senses.definition: (intransitive) To drag oneself lazily or reluctantly along.
examples: Our parents marched to church and we trailed behind.

senses.definition: To be losing, to be behind in a competition.

quotes.text: Neil Lennon and his players have, in almost no time at all, roared back from trailing Rangers by 15 points in November to ending the year two points clear.

senses.definition: (military) To carry (a firearm) with the breech near the ground and the upper part inclined forward, the piece being held by the right hand near the middle.

senses.definition: The track or indication marking the route followed by something that has passed, such as the footprints of animal on land or the contrail of an airplane in the sky.
A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.

examples: Politicians are on the campaign trail in preparation for this year's election.
